reader.requirement: At --std 85 a file description entry admits IS EXTERNAL and IS GLOBAL with the meanings of §1985:X.4.5 and X.4.6: an EXTERNAL FD shares one file connector and record area across the run unit, and a GLOBAL FD makes the file-name and its records visible to contained programs. Every other FD clause keeps its own module's rules.

edition-consulted.switches: at 85, refuses with COBOL0900 the 2002 'AS literal' externalized-name phrase after EXTERNAL (construct ExternalizedNameAs2002)

reader.edition-search: Apart from the AS gate, a grep for Edition, Year and Constructs in LinkageBinder.cs#CallBindExternalAndGlobal and DataBinder.ClausePlacement.cs found nothing; the EXTERNAL/GLOBAL FD binding is one arm at every edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: 2002+ admits EXTERNAL AS literal-1 on the FD, and 85 refuses it. Sharing and visibility do not differ.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f06_07 covers one shape. The probes add an EXTERNAL FD shared by two separately compiled programs, a GLOBAL FD used by contained programs, a failed OPEN on an EXTERNAL GLOBAL file, and the SAME RECORD AREA refusal.

probes.printed: PCLOSE closes the file PWRITE opened (STAT=00); PWRITE re-opens it INPUT and reads ROW-ONE STAT=00
probes.expected: one external file connector shared across separately compiled programs (§1985:X.4.5.4 GR4)

probes.printed: INNER WROTE STAT=00 / OUTER READ BYINNER / INNER2 READ BYINNER STAT=00
probes.expected: the GLOBAL file-name and record are usable in contained programs (§1985:X.4.6.4 GR1-2)

probes.printed: OPEN STAT=35, then the contained program's READ gives STAT=47 and no AT END
probes.expected: a failed OPEN gives status 35; a READ on the unopened file gives 47

probes.printed: COBOL0900: the AS externalized-name phrase requires COBOL-2002
COBOL2738: SAME RECORD AREA with a GLOBAL FD refused

reader.notes: This is a pointer rule. It is judged by whether the FD admits the two IPC clauses at 85 and gives them their X-23/X-24 meaning, and both hold. The diagnostics cite §2023 clause numbers at --std 85.

refuter.evidence: §1985:VII.3.2.3 SR2 says 'The clauses which follow file-name-1 may appear in any order' (cite.py OK). Probe r2a_fd_order.cob puts IS GLOBAL and IS EXTERNAL AFTER BLOCK CONTAINS and LABEL RECORDS, in the reverse order: EXIT 0, 'INNER WROTE ST=00 / OUTER READ BYINNR ST=00'. Probe r2c_fd_indexed_global.cob (Format 2) has an indexed FD with IS EXTERNAL IS GLOBAL and a relative FD with IS GLOBAL, both written by a contained program: EXIT 0, 'OUTER READ K02BRAVO ST=00 / OUTER REL REL2 ST2=00'. Probe r2f_fd_report_global.cob (Format 3) has a report-file FD with IS GLOBAL IS EXTERNAL REPORT IS R1 and RD R1 GLOBAL, and the contained program runs GENERATE: EXIT 0, and the file holds HELLO. Probes r2d and r2e (a FILLER record under a GLOBAL or EXTERNAL FD): both COBOL2404, refused per §1985:X.4.3.3 SR5 (cite.py OK). cite.py: OK  §1985:X.4.2.4 GR2  (4.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2.
